newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA SAY ZOLA DEAL NOT COMPLETED YET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA SAY ZOLA DEAL NOT COMPLETED YET.

text.p: Italian club Parma said on Thursday that Chelsea wanted to sign their international striker Gianfranco Zola but a deal had yet to be completed.
Earlier, British and Italian television reported that Zola had signed a two-year contract with the London club in a deal worth around 13 billion lire ($7.8 million).
Parma said they were waiting for the player's response to the Chelsea offer before taking the negotiations any further.

"The player, with his agent, must still meet Chelsea's general manager Colin Hutchinson," said Parma's general manager Michele Uva. "Only then will Zola and the English official announce whether a deal has been reached.
"At that point Parma will be willing to sit down at a table with them to look at Chelsea's definitive offer."
In an earlier statement, Parma said Chelsea had made an "interesting offer" and that contacts had been made between Hutchinson and officials from the serie A club.
If the 30-year-old Sardinian does go to Chelsea he will join compatriot Gianluca Vialli and international team mate Roberto Di Matteo at the club managed by Ruud Gullit.
He will also become the third player in a year to leave Parma for England -- the others were Colombian Faustino Asprilla to Newcastle and Swede Tomas Brolin to Leeds.
Zola said on Wednesday he had problems with Parma, mainly because coach Carlo Ancelotti insisted on seeing him as a right-sided midfielder whereas he wanted to play as an outright striker.
Parma have Italy international Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo, both signed in the close season, as their first-choice strikers.
But Zola said he hoped to overcome his problems and remain at the club he joined in 1993 from Napoli.
With Napoli he won the league title in 1989-90, his first season at the club after joining from minor league clubs in his native island of Sardinia.
The stocky Zola has been a stalwart of the Italian national team for some years and was one of the few players who stood out in their 2-1 defeat by Bosnia in Sarajevo on Wednesday.
He has scored 49 goals in 102 league games for Parma, helping them to UEFA Cup and Cup Winners' Cup triumphs.
